broadcasts.message: normalize.js unchanged: NFKC, lowercase, collapse all Unicode whitespace to one ASCII space, trim. Non-string returns ''. My output feeds directly into tokenizer's regex. No shadowing of injected deps. Ready for remaining rounds.

Tokenizer remains as specified: calls normalize(text), extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes, returns array in input order. Empty input yields empty array. No changes needed this round.

All three files are consistent. pipeline.js remains as before: processText calls tokenize once, builds null-prototype frequencies to handle constructor, preserves first-seen unique order, and joins tokens with spaces. No changes needed. Ready for next rounds.

Non-string returns ''. No changes needed. Peers' tokenizer and pipeline are compatible with my output. Continue as is.
private_memories.tokenizer: Round 2: Tokenizer unchanged and correct. Spec: tokenize calls injected normalize(text), regex matches ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior apostrophes. Empty/non-string returns empty array. Normalizer and pipeline are compatible. No changes needed.
private_memories.integrator: Round 2: Shared code matches spec. normalize handles non-string by returning ''; tokenizer calls normalize and returns match array or []. My pipeline is unchanged and correct. Keep using Object.create(null) for frequencies to handle prototype names. Guard against tokenize returning non-array (defensive). Do not shadow tokenize/normalize. No changes needed this round. Potential future: if tokenizer changes to return frozen array, still fine. If normalize changes whitespace handling, tokenizer handles. Faithful processing: no filtering, no stopwords, preserve order. Next rounds: re-evaluate if peers change their files.
